nodes.summary: Let $V$ be a list of distinct vertices, and let $r$ and $F$ be such that $r$ followed by the vertices of the forest $F$ in preorder is a permutation of $V$ (the tree with root $r$ and subtree forest $F$ spans $V$). Then the list returned by `APPROX-TSP-TOUR` on $r$ and $F$ is a tour of $V$: it is a permutation of $V$.
nodes.title: The approximate TSP tour is a tour

nodes.summary: For every root $r$ and forest $F$, the running time of `APPROX-TSP-TOUR` on $r$ and $F$ equals the length of the list of $r$ followed by the vertices of $F$ in preorder: one unit per vertex of the returned tour.
nodes.title: Running time of `APPROX-TSP-TOUR`

nodes.summary: Let $d$ be a cost function on vertices with values in a linearly ordered additive commutative monoid that is symmetric, zero on the diagonal, nonnegative and satisfies the triangle inequality. Let $V$ be a list of vertices, let the tree with root $r$ and subtree forest $F$ be a minimum spanning tree of $V$ for $d$, and let $H$ be a tour of $V$. Then the cost under $d$ of the closed tour returned by…
nodes.title: APPROX-TSP-TOUR on a given minimum spanning tree costs at most twice any tour

nodes.summary: CLRS `APPROX-TSP-TOUR`, steps 3 and 4: given a root $r$ and a forest $F$ (the subtrees of a spanning tree with root $r$), return the tour that lists $r$ followed by the vertices of $F$ in preorder. As a timed computation it charges one unit for $r$ and one unit for each vertex visited by the preorder walk of $F$.
nodes.title: The APPROX-TSP-TOUR algorithm

nodes.summary: Let $p$ assign to each vertex of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ either a parent or nothing. For $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and a vertex $v$, the forest below $v$ of depth $k$ is empty when $k = 0$. For depth $k + 1$ it has one tree for each child $c$ of $v$ (each vertex whose parent is $v$), in increasing order of $c$, namely $c$ with the forest below $c$ of depth $k$ as its subtrees.
nodes.title: Forest of a parent array below a vertex

nodes.summary: The forest of a list $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n$ of vertices is the path $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n$: $x_1$ is its only top-level vertex and each $x_{i+1}$ is the only child of $x_i$. The empty list gives the empty forest.
nodes.title: Path as a forest

nodes.summary: Let $p$ assign to each vertex of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ either a parent or nothing. The children of a vertex $v$ are the vertices $c$ whose parent $p(c)$ is $v$, listed in increasing order.
nodes.title: Children in a parent array

nodes.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the complete graph on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ as a directed adjacency: the vertices are listed in increasing order, and the neighbours of each vertex $u$ are all vertices other than $u$, in increasing order.
nodes.title: Complete graph as an ordered adjacency

nodes.summary: Let $p$ assign to each vertex of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ either a parent or nothing, forming a parent tree with root $r$, and let a step up move a vertex to its parent, leaving a vertex without parent in place. Then every vertex $u \ne r$ lies strictly below $r$, at most $n$ levels down: for some $j < n$, the vertex reached from $u$ after $j$ steps up has parent $r$.
nodes.title: Every non-root vertex lies below the root

nodes.summary: Let $p$ assign to each vertex of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ either a parent or nothing, and let a step up move a vertex to its parent, leaving a vertex without parent in place. For $k \in \mathbb{N}$, a vertex $u$ lies strictly below a vertex $v$, at most $k$ levels down, when for some $j < k$ the vertex reached from $u$ after $j$ steps up has parent $v$.
nodes.title: Descendant within $k$ levels

nodes.summary: A rooted forest with vertices in $\alpha$ is either empty, or consists of a first tree with root $v$, whose subtrees form a forest (the children of $v$), followed by a forest of the remaining trees (the siblings of $v$).
nodes.title: Rooted forest in left-child right-sibling form

nodes.summary: A cost function $d$ assigning to each pair of vertices a value in a linearly ordered additive commutative monoid is metric when, for all vertices $x$, $y$, $z$, it is symmetric, $d(x, y) = d(y, x)$, zero on the diagonal, $d(x, x) = 0$, nonnegative, $0 \le d(x, y)$, and satisfies the triangle inequality $d(x, z) \le d(x, y) + d(y, z)$.
nodes.title: Metric cost function

nodes.summary: Let $d$ be a cost function on the vertices with values in a linearly ordered additive commutative monoid. The tree with root $r$ and subtree forest $F$ is a minimum spanning tree of a list $V$ of vertices for $d$ when it is a spanning tree of $V$ (the vertices of $V$ are distinct and the list of $r$ followed by the vertices of $F$ in preorder is a permutation of $V$) and, for every vertex $r'$ and forest $F'$ such…
nodes.title: Minimum spanning tree of a vertex list

nodes.summary: Let $p$ assign to each vertex of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ either a parent or nothing, forming a parent tree with root $r$. Then $r$ together with the forest below $r$ of depth $n$ built from $p$ is a spanning tree of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$: $r$ followed by the vertices of the forest in preorder lists every vertex exactly once.
nodes.title: The forest of a parent tree spans all vertices

nodes.summary: Let $W$ be a linearly ordered type with a zero and a commutative addition, let $d$ assign a weight in $W$ to each ordered pair of vertices of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, and let $r$ be a vertex. Then $r$ together with Prim's forest for $d$ and $r$ is a spanning tree of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$: $r$ followed by the vertices of the forest in preorder lists every vertex exactly once.
nodes.title: Prim's forest spans all vertices

nodes.summary: The tree with root $r$ and subtree forest $F$ is a spanning tree of a list $V$ of vertices when the vertices of $V$ are distinct and the list of $r$ followed by the vertices of $F$ in preorder is a permutation of $V$: the vertices of the tree are those of $V$, each exactly once.
nodes.title: Rooted spanning tree of a vertex list

nodes.summary: A list $H$ is a tour of a list $V$ of vertices when the vertices of $V$ are distinct and $H$ is a permutation of $V$: $H$ lists each vertex of $V$ exactly once and nothing else.
nodes.title: Tour of a vertex list

nodes.summary: For all vertices $u, v$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, $v$ is listed among the neighbours of $u$ in the complete graph as an ordered adjacency if and only if $u$ and $v$ are adjacent in the complete simple graph on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, that is, $u \ne v$.
nodes.title: Neighbours in the complete adjacency

nodes.summary: Let $W$ be a linearly ordered type with a zero and a commutative addition, let $d$ assign a weight in $W$ to each ordered pair of vertices of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, and let $r$ be a vertex. Then Prim's parent array for $d$ from $r$ is a parent tree with root $r$: $r$ has no parent, and every vertex reaches $r$ after finitely many steps up, where a step up moves a vertex to its parent and leaves a vertex without…
nodes.title: Prim's parent array is a parent tree

nodes.summary: Let $p$ assign to each vertex of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ either a parent or nothing, and let a step up move a vertex to its parent, leaving a vertex without parent in place. The parent array $p$ is a parent tree with root $r$ when $r$ has no parent and every vertex reaches $r$ after finitely many steps up.
nodes.title: Parent tree

nodes.summary: Let $d$ be a cost function on the vertices with values in a linearly ordered additive commutative monoid, which is symmetric, zero on the diagonal, nonnegative, and satisfies the triangle inequality. For a vertex $p$ and lists $A$, $B$ of vertices, the cost of the walk that starts at $p$, visits $A$ and then $B$ in order and returns to $p$ is at most the cost of the walk from $p$ through $A$ back to $p$ plus the…
nodes.title: Shortcutting a closed walk through its base point

nodes.summary: Let $d$ be a cost function on the vertices with values in a linearly ordered additive commutative monoid, which is symmetric, zero on the diagonal, nonnegative, and satisfies the triangle inequality. For vertices $v$, $p$ and a list $C$ of vertices, the cost of the walk from $v$ through $C$ ending at $p$ is at most the cost of the walk from $v$ through $C$ ending back at $v$, plus $d(v, p)$.
nodes.title: Rerouting the end of a walk

nodes.summary: Let $d$ be a cost function on the vertices with values in a linearly ordered additive commutative monoid, which is symmetric, zero on the diagonal, nonnegative, and satisfies the triangle inequality. For vertices $q$, $p$ and a list $L$ of vertices, the cost of the walk from $q$ through $L$ is at most $d(q, p)$ plus the cost of the walk from $p$ through $L$.
nodes.title: Changing the starting vertex of a walk

nodes.summary: Let $d$ be a cost function on the vertices with values in a linearly ordered additive commutative monoid, which is symmetric, zero on the diagonal, nonnegative, and satisfies the triangle inequality. For a forest $F$ and a vertex $p$, let $w$ be the weight of $F$ hanging below $p$: the total cost of the edges joining $p$ to the top-level vertices of $F$ and each vertex of $F$ to its children. Then the cost of the…
nodes.title: The closed preorder walk below a vertex costs at most twice the forest

nodes.summary: Let $d$ be a cost function on the vertices with values in an additive commutative monoid. For a vertex $x$ and a list $L = [y_1, \dots, y_n]$ of vertices, the cost of the walk from $x$ through $L$ is $d(x, y_1) + d(y_1, y_2) + \dots + d(y_{n-1}, y_n)$, and $0$ when $L$ is empty.
nodes.title: Cost of a walk

nodes.summary: For every list $L$ of vertices, the preorder of the forest of $L$ (the path through the vertices of $L$ in order) is $L$ itself.
nodes.title: Preorder of a path

nodes.summary: For every forest $F$ and every list $a$ of vertices, the preorder walk of $F$ with accumulator $a$ returns the vertices of $F$ in preorder followed by $a$.
nodes.title: Result of the preorder walk with an accumulator

nodes.summary: For a forest $F$ and a list $a$ of vertices, this is the timed computation defined as follows. On the empty forest it returns $a$ at no cost. On a forest with first root $v$, children forest $C$ and sibling forest $S$, it charges one time unit, walks $S$ with accumulator $a$ to get a list $b$, walks $C$ with accumulator $b$ to get a list $c$, and returns $v$ followed by $c$. It thus returns the vertices of $F$ in…
nodes.title: Preorder walk with an accumulator

nodes.summary: For a forest $F$, the preorder walk of $F$ is the preorder walk of $F$ with the empty list as accumulator: a timed computation that returns the vertices of $F$ in preorder, at one time unit per vertex.
nodes.title: Preorder walk

nodes.summary: The list of the vertices of a forest in preorder: empty for the empty forest, and for a forest with first root $v$, children forest $C$ and sibling forest $S$, the vertex $v$, followed by the preorder of $C$, followed by the preorder of $S$.
nodes.title: Preorder of a forest

nodes.summary: Given costs $d(u,v)$ on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with values in a linearly ordered type with a zero and commutative addition, and a root $r$, take Prim's parent array for $d$ and $r$ (Prim's algorithm run from $r$ on the complete graph with edge weights $d(u,v) + d(v,u)$). This forest is the forest of the subtrees below $r$ in that parent array, cut off $n$ levels below $r$, in left-child right-sibling…
nodes.title: Forest of Prim's tree

nodes.summary: Given costs $d(u,v)$ on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with values in a linearly ordered type with a zero and commutative addition, and a root $r$, this is the parent array returned by Prim's algorithm run from $r$ on the complete graph on these vertices, with the weight of the edge $\{u, v\}$ equal to $d(u,v) + d(v,u)$: it sends each vertex to its parent, or to no parent.
nodes.title: Prim's parent array on the complete graph

nodes.summary: Let $d(u,v)$ be real costs on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, let $r$ be a vertex, and weigh each edge $\{u, v\}$ by $d(u,v) + d(v,u)$. Then Prim's tree for $d$ and $r$ is a tree, and for every tree $H$ on these vertices the total weight of the edges of Prim's tree is at most the total weight of the edges of $H$.
nodes.title: Prim's tree is a minimum spanning tree

nodes.summary: For costs $d(u,v)$ on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with values in any linearly ordered type with a zero and commutative addition, and any root $r$, Prim's tree for $d$ and $r$ is a tree on all of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, that is, a spanning tree of the complete graph.
nodes.title: Prim's tree is a spanning tree

nodes.summary: Given costs $d(u,v)$ on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with values in a linearly ordered type with a zero and commutative addition, and a root $r$, Prim's tree is the simple graph on these vertices in which distinct vertices $u$ and $v$ are adjacent when one of them is the parent of the other in Prim's parent array for $d$ and $r$.
nodes.title: Prim's tree

nodes.summary: For costs $d(u,v)$ on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with values in a linearly ordered type with a zero and commutative addition, and any root $r$, the list returned by APPROX-TSP-TOUR with Prim's tree for $d$ and $r$ is a permutation of $0, 1, \dots, n-1$: it visits every vertex exactly once.
nodes.title: The tour from Prim's tree is a tour

nodes.summary: Let $d$ be a real metric cost on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ (symmetric, zero on the diagonal, nonnegative, and satisfying the triangle inequality), and let $r$ be a vertex. Then the cost of the closed tour through the list returned by APPROX-TSP-TOUR with Prim's tree for $d$ and $r$ is at most twice the cost of the closed tour through $H$, for every list $H$ that visits each of $0, 1, \dots, n-1$ exactly once.
nodes.title: APPROX-TSP-TOUR with Prim's tree is a 2-approximation

nodes.summary: Given costs $d(u,v)$ on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with values in a linearly ordered type with a zero and commutative addition, and a root $r$, the tour is $r$ followed by the vertices of the forest of Prim's tree below $r$ in preorder. Its running time counts one unit per vertex of the tour; running Prim's algorithm and building the forest are not counted.
nodes.title: APPROX-TSP-TOUR with Prim's tree

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a parent array on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ in which the root $r$ has no parent and every chain of parents reaches $r$, and let $w$ assign to each unordered pair $\{u, v\}$ of vertices (possibly $u = v$) a value in a commutative additive monoid. Write $\hat p(u)$ for the parent of $u$, or $u$ itself if $u$ has no parent. Then the sum of $w(e)$ over the edges $e$ of the parent graph (distinct $u$…
nodes.title: Edge sums over a parent tree

nodes.summary: Given costs $d(u,v)$ on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with values in a type with commutative addition, the weight of an unordered pair $\{u, v\}$ is $d(u,v) + d(v,u)$, which does not depend on the order of $u$ and $v$. When $d$ is symmetric this is twice the cost, which leaves minimum spanning trees unchanged.
nodes.title: Symmetrized edge weights

nodes.summary: Let $d$ be a cost function on the vertices with values in a linearly ordered additive commutative monoid that is symmetric, zero on the diagonal, nonnegative and satisfies the triangle inequality. Let $T$ be a rooted tree with root $r$, given by the forest $F$ of the subtrees of $r$, and let $w(T)$ be its weight, the total cost of its edges. Then the closed tour that visits $r$, then the vertices of $F$ in…
nodes.title: The preorder tour costs at most twice the tree

nodes.summary: For a cost function $d$ on the vertices with values in an additive commutative monoid, the cost of the closed tour that visits $x_0, x_1, \dots, x_k$ in order and returns to its first vertex is $\sum_{i=1}^{k} d(x_{i-1}, x_i) + d(x_k, x_0)$. The empty tour costs $0$.
nodes.title: Cost of a closed tour

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a parent array on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, assigning to each vertex $v$ either a parent $p(v)$ or no parent. Then $\operatorname{up}(v)$ is the parent $p(v)$ when $v$ has one, and $v$ itself otherwise, so a root stays put.
nodes.title: One step up a parent array

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a parent array on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, let $d$ be a cost on ordered pairs of vertices with values in an additive commutative monoid, and let $\operatorname{up}(u)$ be the parent of $u$, or $u$ itself if $u$ has no parent. For every $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and every vertex $v$, let $F$ be the forest of the subtrees of the children of $v$ in $p$, cut off $k$ levels below $v$. Then the weight under…
nodes.title: Weight of the forest built from a parent array

nodes.summary: Let $d$ be a cost function on the vertices with values in a linearly ordered additive commutative monoid that is symmetric, zero on the diagonal, nonnegative and satisfies the triangle inequality. Let $V$ be a list of distinct vertices. Let $T$ be a minimum spanning tree of $V$ for $d$: a rooted tree whose vertices are the elements of $V$, each once, whose weight (the total cost of its edges) is at most that of…
nodes.title: A minimum spanning tree costs at most any tour

nodes.summary: For a cost function $d$ and a vertex $p$, the weight of a forest hanging below $p$ is the total cost of its tree edges: each top-level vertex $v$ is joined to $p$ by an edge of cost $d(p, v)$, and each vertex $u$ is joined to each of its children $c$ by an edge of cost $d(u, c)$. The empty forest has weight $0$.
nodes.title: Weight of a forest below a vertex
Computer Science

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
